title: One-day endpoint delay bounds permit both warmth slope signs in four Swiss beech samples in 1961-2020
abstract: We tested whether possible reporting delays can reverse the link between autumn warmth and the time from 50% leaf colour to 50% leaf fall. We used 4,538 paired records at 124 Swiss beech stations in two regions and two periods from 1961 to 2020. Models removed station effects and station trends. Separate delays of zero to one day at each endpoint permit both slope signs in all four samples. The minimum continuous delay budget that reaches zero ranges from 0.26 to 0.87 day. These are exact fixed-record bounds under assumed late reports, not measured visit errors or confidence intervals. Reported-date slopes range from -0.25 to +0.65 days per C; none passes correction for four tests. The bounds allow worst-case links between delay and weather. Common delays at both endpoints cancel. Missing visits, selected stations, coarse weather and one species limit inference. We infer no causal climate or pollution effect. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and figures support reproduction.

display.caption: Exact possible slope ranges under separate endpoint delay budgets. These are fixed-record bounds, not confidence intervals.
Reported-date slopes and ordinary 95% intervals. No gap test passes Holm correction for four samples.

citations.reason: Prior Swiss interval analysis informs the follow-up. Records overlap. We add endpoint-delay bounds for a mean-warmth model with station trends.
